/-!
# Conjecture 10.71

by V. A. Churkin

Is it true that the centralizer of any automorphism (any finite set of automorphisms) in the
automorphism group of a free group of finite rank is a finitely presented group? This is true in
the case of rank 2 and in the case of inner automorphisms for any finite rank.

The free group of finite rank $n$ is modelled as `FreeGroup (Fin n)` and its automorphism group
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ as `MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n))`. Mathlib has no notion of a finitely
presented group, so one is defined here: a group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ for finitely many generators $x_i$ and
finitely many relators $r_j$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$, i.e. to a quotient of the free
group on `Fin n` by the normal closure of a finite set of relators.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.FG (only finite generation, strictly weaker); PresentedGroup (used as the building block); Module.FinitePresentation (module analogue, not applicable to groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.71».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a 'finitely presented group' predicate (only Group.FG, and Module.FinitePresentation / RingHom.FinitePresentation for modules/rings). Defined as ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))), Nonempty (PresentedGroup ↑rels ≃* G), i.e. G ≅ ⟨x_1..x_n | r_1..r_m⟩ with finitely many generators and relators. Accompanied by a proved API lemma (IsFinitelyPresented.fg : finitely presented → Group.FG) and a proved test (FreeGroup (Fin n) is finitely presented).

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$, i.e. to a quotient of the free
group on `Fin n` by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (FreeGroup (Fin n)) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of _, Set.finite_range _⟩
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_of_surjective (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _)
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective
blocks.docstring: A finitely presented group is finitely generated.

claims.decomposer_note: Primary yes/no question read for a single automorphism: for every n : ℕ and every φ ∈ Aut(FreeGroup (Fin n)) = MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)), the subgroup Subgroup.centralizer {φ} is a finitely presented group; Mathlib has no 'finitely presented group' predicate, so a bespoke definition via PresentedGroup with finitely many generators and relators is needed, and ranks 0,1 are trivially fine so no restriction n ≥ 2 is required (though harmless).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot identically: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ φ : MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)), IsFinitelyPresented ↥(Subgroup.centralizer {φ}). Verified that Subgroup.centralizer {φ} is the subgroup of automorphisms commuting with φ and that PresentedGroup rels is FreeGroup ⧸ normalClosure rels, so the bespoke predicate is the standard notion of finite presentability (up to isomorphism). Ranks 0 and 1 give finite groups, so no domain restriction is needed. c04 chosen as the base because it adds proven API/test lemmas (finitely presented ⇒ Group.FG; free groups are finitely presented) for the bespoke definition, as CONTRIBUTING requests.

claims.reviewer_why: All candidates equivalent: for every n and every Finset S of automorphisms each lying in MulAut.conj.range (verified: MulAut.conj g x = g * x * g⁻¹, so the range is exactly Inn(F_n)), the centralizer is finitely presented; research solved. For n ≥ 2 this is the pointwise stabilizer of finitely many elements (F_n has trivial center), finitely presented by McCool's theorem; n ≤ 1 is finite. /-!
# Conjecture 10.71

by V. A. Churkin

Is it true that the centralizer of any automorphism (any finite set of automorphisms) in the
automorphism group of a free group of finite rank is a finitely presented group? This is true in
the case of rank 2 and in the case of inner automorphisms for any finite rank.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.71»

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$, i.e. to a quotient of the free
group on `Fin n` by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (FreeGroup (Fin n)) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of _, Set.finite_range _⟩
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_of_surjective (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _)
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/-- The free group of finite rank is finitely presented (by the empty set of relators). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := by
  refine ⟨n, ∅, ⟨(QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq ?_).trans QuotientGroup.quotientBot⟩⟩
  exact le_bot_iff.mp (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp))

/--
Is it true that the centralizer of any automorphism in the automorphism group
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ of a free group $F_n$ of finite rank $n$ is a finitely presented
group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.71» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsFinitelyPresented (Subgroup.centralizer {φ}) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that the centralizer of any finite set of automorphisms in the automorphism group
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ of a free group $F_n$ of finite rank $n$ is a finitely presented
group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.71».variants.finite_set : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)))),
      IsFinitelyPresented (Subgroup.centralizer (S : Set (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n))))) := by
  sorry

/--
The centralizer of any finite set of automorphisms (in particular, of any single automorphism)
in the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(F_2)$ of the free group of rank $2$ is a finitely
presented group.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.71».variants.rank_two (S : Finset (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin 2)))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (Subgroup.centralizer (S : Set (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin 2))))) := by
  sorry

/--
For every finite rank $n$, the centralizer of any finite set of inner automorphisms (in
particular, of any single inner automorphism) in the automorphism group
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ is a finitely presented group.
Here an automorphism is inner if it is conjugation by some element of $F_n$, i.e. lies in the
range of `MulAut.conj`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.71».variants.inner (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n))))
    (hS : ∀ φ ∈ S, φ ∈ MulAut.conj.range) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (Subgroup.centralizer (S : Set (MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n))))) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.71»

items: Aut(F_n) is modelled as MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)); ranks n = 0, 1 are included (∀ n : ℕ) since the statement says 'finite rank' and these cases are trivially true, so no n ≥ 2 restriction is imposed.
'Finite set of automorphisms' is a Finset of MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)), and the centralizer is Subgroup.centralizer of its coercion to Set.

Both known special cases (rank 2, inner automorphisms) are stated in the finite-set form, since 'This is true...' refers to the whole preceding question including the parenthetical; each subsumes the single-automorphism form via S = {φ}. For inner automorphisms the finite-set form is the stabilizer of a finite tuple of elements (n ≥ 2), finitely presented by McCool's theorem; for n ≤ 1 Aut(F_n) is finite.
Inner automorphisms are formalized as elements of (MulAut.conj : F_n →* MulAut F_n).range, via a hypothesis ∀ φ ∈ S, φ ∈ MulAut.conj.range.

IsFinitelyPresented uses Fin n as generator index type and a Finset of relators; this is equivalent to the usual definition over an arbitrary finite generating type by PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup. The definition lives in the problem file (all work confined to the candidate file), though it is generic enough to move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
The two solved variants carry @[category research solved] with sorry bodies and no formal_proof attribute, since no formal proof exists.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compiled and produced mathematically identical formalizations of all four slots (same bespoke IsFinitelyPresented via PresentedGroup on Fin n generators with a Finset of relators, same MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin n)) model, same Finset/centralizer encoding, same MulAut.conj.range encoding of inner automorphisms); no candidate omitted any slot. The final file is c04 with one cosmetic edit (removing an inferable named-argument annotation in the inner slot). Judgment calls a human should be aware of: (1) The two 'known case' slots are stated in the finite-set form (as the decomposition table directs and as the sentence 'This is true…' naturally reads); for the inner case this is a known theorem (McCool), for rank 2 the notebook's assertion is taken at face value — if a reviewer prefers the weaker single-automorphism reading of the rank-2 claim, replace S : Finset by a singleton. (2) The two open slots carry independent answer(sorry) and no formal link between the two answers is asserted. (3) Ranks 0 and 1 are included since they are trivially fine. (4) The bespoke IsFinitelyPresented is kept in the problem file; it is generic enough to move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib in a real PR. Final file compiles with only the four expected 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
